402.t: Reel 2: WPA band photo from the Italian Hall
402.s: Interviewer opens reel 2 with a picture of the original WPA band, formerly Ray's band, made at the Italian Hall.
402.ch: WPA band and 1930s New Orleans bands
402.q: And whose band is it? You know Joe Maxey? I know him, yes, I met him. Trombone, I know him. Well, this is the original WPA band, in fact it was the EO Ray band before the WPA.

402.t: Sam Majada and the police band; Tony Fougerat and Jeff Riddick
402.s: Sal and the interviewer identify members of Sam Majada's band and Sal says he played with Tony Fougerat and Jeff Riddick, including a job in Mobile.
402.ch: WPA band and 1930s New Orleans bands
402.q: I've seen that picture with the police convention. Well, that's a band. I used to what he's seeing. I got that, I think. Did Raymond play? Yeah, Raymond.

769.t: Playing with Bud Russell, Foster Lewis and Dude
769.s: Bud Russell brings him into a band with Eddie Dawson, Dude, a trombonist, a saxophonist and a banjo player, working Sundays at Galvez and Iberville.
769.q: Well, there was Bud Russel, Baby Brewster, and this boy Frog and myself, it was four of us. Yeah. Well, we didn't say hi to Russel because he didn't want to be hired out, you know, because he was already with this other band. And, well, we played practically all over the city on Sunday nights, but…

769.t: Foster Lewis and Dude's band and the player Yalla
769.s: He lists the first band he played with and says little of Yalla.
769.q: Yeah I spoke about them on the earlier reel. I used to play with them. The first band I played with was Foster Lewis and Dude. Because Roussel, or Bud Roussel was playing bass with them. That was the first band I would play with.

761.t: First band and Sam Morgan's players
761.s: He names his first band and the players of Sam Morgan's and Rene's bands he mixed with.
761.q: Yeah, On All The Past. Yeah, On All The Past. And I mixed it with Rene, Sam Morgan. I was having the majority of them afterwards, after I found out I could play, they used me. At that time, they was using Judge E. Parker. You know Judge E. Parker? Uh-huh. And a father by the name of Edward Johnson,…

922.s: Lineup of the Tuxedo band from 1910 as seen in Ridgely's photograph, and later members.
922.q: I don't remember the exact month or date, but I did get that information from the picture, which William Ridgely, maybe Ridgely had died not so long ago, he had of the Tuxedo band. And that original Tuxedo band, it was Ridgely on trombone, Celestine on trumpet. My father was playing drum, the…

629.t: Bands he played in: Excelsior, Bloom, Robichaux, Moret, Independent
629.s: Picou runs through bands including Manuel Perez's Excelsior, Joe Bloom's orchestra, sixteen years with Robichaux, George Moret, Duconge, and his own Golden Leaf and Independent bands.
629.q: One of the best sharp play we had in New Orleans. He used to hit a high note in a parade because he had way up above. He was Carlos Tower. Talk about that? Yes, indeed.

192.t: First bands: Golden Rule band, Young Tuxedo Band lineup
192.s: He lists his first band's members and its change into the Young Tuxedo Band with its personnel.
192.q: No, relations at all. Bush Hall. No, he had no relation at all. Let's see. We formed a...we first called the band the Golden Rule New Orleans Jazz Band, the Golden Rule Band. And we said we had Paul Bones, Eddie, Morrell, Lawrence Morrell, and we didn't have no piano during them days with the…

1006.t: After the war: Young Olympia, Young Tuxedo and Bob Lyons bands
1006.s: Alexis worked twice with the Young Olympia, then the Young Tuxedo band (Celestin's overflow), then Bob Lyons' band replacing Willie Edwards, and recalls its members.
1006.ch: New Orleans bands after the war
1006.q: Young Olympia band twice. Then the Young Tuxedo band, which Doc Oynos the bass player was the band. Freddie Babu was the trombone player.

950.t: Old Tuxedo Band days and ceasing to play out in the 1920s
950.s: He recalls playing with the Tuxedo Band, Oscar Randall and others, stopping playing out in the 1920s and now playing occasionally with the Chalice family.
950.q: Well, that's what I did. I got my own arrangement copyrighted, you see. And, oh, it went on nice, it went on nice. We should sing that. Yeah. And I was fixing to get the boys together, because I, very few musicians I know now, they all, you're all my old musician friends, they're all gone. I…

198.t: The Golden Rule, Imperial, Superior and Boys in Blue bands
198.s: Barnes names bands of the period and their leaders: Buddy Petit's Boys in Blue, Sugar Johnny's Imperial, and the Golden Rule with swapping personnel.
198.q: Well, we all put, partly was in the, hooked up with the same band, cause, uh, you see, in them things we had, let's see, you had the Golden Rule, had the Golden Rule, had the Imperial, you had the Superior, you had the Boys in Blue.

308.t: Golden Rule becomes the Young Tuxedo Band
308.s: The band played local balls, became the Young Tuxedo Band, then spread into orchestras with Lloyd Cottrell and Don Albert.
308.q: Well, it was all local, balls, banquets we call them, every Monday, regular dance. And then that band stretched out from the Golden Rule, they went into the Young Tuxedo Band with it.
